front.title: The Delegation Logic Calculus (DLC) Token: A Self-Verifying Authorization Format with Logical, Cryptographic, and IFC Semantics

abstract.t: This document specifies the Delegation Logic Calculus (DLC) Token, a wire format for authorization tokens whose validation simultaneously checks logical entailment, cryptographic authenticity of every principal in the delegation chain, and the information-flow-control (IFC) label algebra of every claim. A DLC token is a content-addressed Merkle DAG whose nodes carry proof-term structure, COSE_Sign1 signatures, and IFC labels; verification is O(|M| log |Keyring|) in proof and keyring size and requires no network access. This specification defines the CBOR wire format, the verification algorithm, and the interoperability requirements with W3C Verifiable Credentials (via the JSON-LD context at dlc.coproduct.dev/contexts/dlc-v1) and OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693). Four mechanized Lean 4 theorems (T1 decidability, T2 cryptographic correspondence, T3 non-interference, T4 obligation soundness) accompany this specification at the cited reference implementation.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The agent-economy authorization landscape in 2026 is fragmented. OAuth 2.0 token exchange defines token composition operationally but assigns it no formal meaning; chain splicing was reported as a real vulnerability in 2026. The on-behalf-of draft introduces actor and principal claims without a calculus that says what their composition denotes. Capability tokens (macaroons, biscuits) attenuate algebraically but lack obligation, IFC, and proof-of- non-interference.
DLC unifies these concerns. A DLC token is simultaneously:

li.t: a proof term in a decidable modal-linear-temporal authorization logic (the calculus);
a Merkle-DAG-addressed wire object whose subtree hashes enable selective recomputation and cross-organizational caching at IFC-controlled boundaries.

section.t: This document specifies the wire format and verification algorithm. The metatheory lives in a companion Lean 4 development at .

section.name: Terminology
section.t:
The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

Principal: an atomic identity bound to a public key. Principals compose via the operators & (conjunctive consent), | (disjunctive consent), and U+2293 SQUARE CAP ("acting as", associative but not commutative).
Proof Term: a tree-structured object built from the 22 typing rules of the DLC calculus. Leaves are signatures or variable references; interior nodes are rule applications.
DLC Token: the CBOR serialization of a proof term plus its claimed type, IFC label, and obligation set.

section.name: Wire Format
section.t: A DLC token MUST be a COSE_Sign1 envelope whose payload is a CBOR-encoded ProofTerm structure. The protected header MUST include the alg parameter set to EdDSA and a content-type of "application/dlc+cbor".

section.name: ProofTerm CBOR Structure
section.t: The CBOR encoding follows the deterministic-encoding rules of Section 4.2.1, ensuring canonical byte representation. The detailed schema is given in the ABNF appendix of this draft.

section.name: Canonical Form
section.t: Two DLC tokens that encode the same proof term MUST produce identical bytes after canonical encoding. This is enforced by the encoder; verifiers MUST reject any token whose bytes are not in canonical form.

section.name: Verification Algorithm
section.t: Verification proceeds as a single bottom-up traversal of the ProofTerm tree. At each node, the verifier:

li.t: validates the node's CBOR canonical encoding;
combines child results to compute the node's IFC label as the lattice join of the children's labels.

section.t: Total time complexity is O(|M| log |Keyring|), with the log factor from hash-indexed keyring lookup.

section.name: W3C Verifiable Credentials Integration
section.t: A DLC token MAY be embedded as a Verifiable Credential by wrapping its CBOR payload in a JOSE or COSE envelope per and adding the JSON-LD context at https://dlc.coproduct.dev/contexts/dlc-v1.jsonld. The five context terms (DlcAffirmationCredential, delegationChain, obligationSet, ifcLabel, timeWindow) map to the proof term's top-level structure.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The cryptographic correspondence theorem (T2 in the companion Lean development) states that the wire-format verification algorithm succeeds if and only if the underlying proof term is well-typed in the DLC calculus. This rules out confused-deputy attacks , RFC 8693 chain splicing, and JWT confusion attacks (in which a verifier accepts an HS256 token under an RS256 expectation by treating the public key as the HMAC secret), because any such attack would be a proof distinguishing the logical and cryptographic typing judgments.

Long-term-key compromise is modeled as an explicit LtkReveal event in the symbolic models (Tamarin and ProVerif). The secrecy_ltk lemma proves that an honest principal's private key never leaks unless explicitly revealed by that principal.

Time-bound delegations rely on a verifiable time anchor (drand or a NIST randomness beacon). Implementations MUST reject any token whose claimed time window cannot be substantiated against a fresh anchor; clock skew on the verifier is not a substitute.

The verifier MUST NOT contact the network during validation. Keyrings are obtained out-of-band (e.g. via JWKS endpoints cached locally). This "trust no operator" inversion is explicitly tested in the reference implementation.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests IANA to register the following:

li.t: A new media type "application/dlc+cbor" in the IANA Media Types Registry per the procedures of .
A new COSE Header Parameter "dlc-version" (a positive integer) in the COSE Header Parameters registry per .
A new entry in the JSON Web Token Claims registry for "dlc_proof" (a base64url-encoded DLC token).

section.t: Detailed registration templates are provided in the next revision of this draft.
